A heavyweight in the S&P 500, Chevron jumped during the latest session and now trades above the average price objective set by rating firms. Chevron is an integrated energy company that explores for, develops, produces, transports, and markets crude oil and natural gas. Its upstream business finds and pumps hydrocarbons from fields around the world, while its downstream operations refine crude into fuels and manufacture lubricants, petrochemicals, and fuel additives. That integration gives Chevron balance across the energy cycle, since refining margins sometimes improve when crude prices fall. The company also funds lower-carbon businesses, including renewable fuels, carbon capture and storage, and hydrogen. With operations spanning several continents, Chevron is one of the largest and most closely watched energy sector companies in the world. Chevron's latest advance stood out for a company of its size and steadiness. Shares climbed sharply and finished near their intraday high, though trading activity ran somewhat below a typical day. The stock now sits well above both its short-term and long-term moving averages, with the short-term average itself well above the long-term one, the hallmark of a sustained uptrend. That momentum is notable because Chevron's beta is low, meaning it usually moves far less than the broader market. When a stock this steady moves this much, it typically reflects a genuine shift in how the market views its prospects. Chevron's share price has now climbed above the average price objective across rating firms, a sign that the rally has outpaced older forecasts. Fresh revisions are catching up. One firm raised its price objective meaningfully, while another increased its full-year earnings forecast. Models that track estimate changes suggest conditions favor another earnings beat when Chevron next reports, with year-over-year growth expected. The consensus leans moderately favorable, with one top-tier rating, a large majority of positive views, a handful of neutral stances, and a single bearish rating. Even so, the average objective has not yet caught up with the stock. Chevron's most recent quarter delivered a dramatic outperformance.  Earnings per share beat consensus estimates by a wide margin and more than tripled compared with the same quarter last year. Revenue also topped forecasts and jumped by more than half year over year, a striking increase that partly reflects a larger asset base following a major acquisition, alongside firmer energy prices. Return on equity and net margin both sit at moderate levels. Full-year forecasts call for strong earnings, and the coming release will show whether that momentum carried into the latest quarter. Chevron plans to apply the operating model it refined in the Permian Basin of West Texas and New Mexico to Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale region, backed by a large-scale, multiyear spending plan. In the Permian, Chevron learned to drill longer wells, standardize development, and squeeze more oil from each acre through better recovery techniques. Vaca Muerta is one of the largest shale formations outside North America but remains less developed. If Chevron can replicate its Permian efficiency there, the region could become a meaningful source of long-term production growth, diversifying its shale exposure beyond the United States. Chevron is reportedly considering divesting a package of mature assets in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. Older offshore fields often require rising maintenance spending while producing less oil over time, making them better suited to smaller operators that specialize in squeezing value from aging infrastructure. Proceeds could be redirected toward newer deepwater projects and other higher-growth opportunities. That approach reflects disciplined capital allocation: shedding assets with declining returns to fund those with stronger long-term prospects. It also shows Chevron reshaping its portfolio rather than simply adding to it. Chevron has long been one of the most reliable dividend payers in the energy sector, maintaining its payout through multiple oil price downturns. The annualized  dividend yield sits at a solid level, though it has narrowed somewhat as the share price climbed. The payout ratio is moderately high, absorbing a meaningful share of earnings, which leaves less cushion if oil prices fall sharply. Chevron's strong balance sheet and integrated business help support the dividend through downturns, but its growth will ultimately depend on sustained earnings from both existing operations and new projects. Recent rating activity shows forecasters catching up at different speeds. One firm upgraded Chevron to a moderately favorable view, another reaffirmed a favorable rating with a solid objective, and a third raised its objective alongside an outperform rating. Not every move was positive. One firm trimmed its objective while keeping an outperform stance, and another cut its objective while maintaining an equal weight view. That mix explains why the average objective trails the share price. Unless more firms raise their numbers after the upcoming results, Chevron will continue trading ahead of its consensus outlook. title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. XOM stock has gained more than 48% year-to-date, while CVX and MPC stocks have surged more than 47% and 200%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. U.S. stock futures climbed into positive territory late Monday as technology stocks rebounded after a sharp selloff last week. Meanwhile, markets are keenly watching the third-quarter (Q3) earnings season unfold, with about 70 S&P 500 companies slated to report earnings this week. As of 11:13 p.m. EDT, Dow futures were up about 0.25%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.21% and the Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.15%. On Monday, the three benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Nasdaq Composite led the climb, adding more than 290 points to close 1.11% higher. The S&P 500 climbed 0.41% at close, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.07%. Technology and AI stocks were top of mind for markets on Monday as the sector reversed last week's steep selloff. Chip stocks led the climb on Monday. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed up nearly 2%, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) closed up 1.61%. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Micron Technology Inc. (MU) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) all ended the session in green. The run comes ahead of vital Q3 results that will follow this week, which are likely to set the tone for the trajectory of technology shares. “Tech earnings are key this week. Fundamentals are unchanged, but given fragile price action, we turn neutral [on] risk assets and stay neutral duration,” Ajay Rajadhyaksha, global chairman of research at Barclays, said in a note, according to CNBC. Katie Stockton, founder of Fairlead Strategies, reportedly said in a note on Monday that the week will be crucial for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which need to hold support, while noting that a hold is possible amid widespread, short-term oversold conditions. Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) are due to report Q3 results later this week, while multiple other semiconductor and technology companies, including Lam Research (LRCX) and Texas Instruments (TXN), will also post their results. AI-related power companies Bloom Energy (BE) and Valero Energy (VLO), along with big entertainment companies including Netflix Inc. (NFLX), will also announce their quarterly results. Meanwhile, rising oil prices amid growing geopolitical uncertainty have put downward pressure on markets. Brent crude futures expiring in December were trading at $109.88 a barrel, up about 0.3%, while WTI crude futures expiring in November traded at $103.64 per barrel. Economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X, “Oil rose another 2.5% today. It's almost $104. If you think gas prices are high now, just wait until after the midterms when Trump has to turn off the spigots from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to keep it from running dry. Oil could hit $150, sending gas prices to record highs.” Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT): Shares of the president’s media company were in focus late Monday after the stock slipped 8%, its worst single-day drop since February, as President Donald Trump’s approval rating hit a record low. Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN): The company’s stock surged nearly 5% at close on Monday and continued to climb higher overnight after Morgan Stanley raised its price target and named it a ‘Top Pick.’ Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS): The AI hardware and supercomputing company was on the retail radar after shares slipped more than 5% on Monday, extending a broader selloff in the sector from last week. CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV): Shares of the neocloud company fell more than 1% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) all climbed overnight. Meanwhile, U.S. long-dated Treasury yields continued above 5%. At the time of writing, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was 5.138%, and the 30-year Treasury yield was 5.473%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.09% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened lower on Tuesday, with South Korea's KOSPI, Japan’s Nikkei 225, China’s SSE Composite and Australian stocks all trading lower at the time of writing. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Broadcom, Inc. (AVGO) reversed overnight losses to edge up 0.3% late Monday as a 10-year cloud agreement with NTT Docomo did little to ease retail skepticism, with traders seeking a recovery catalyst after CEO Hock Tan’s AI “casino” remarks. AVGO stock rose nearly 2% on Monday to close at $334.59, snapping three straight sessions of losses. Broadcom extended its 2019 deal with Docomo, in which the companies will align their long-term tech roadmaps to advance the private cloud underpinning the Japanese telecom operator’s digital services. The company called it Broadcom Japan’s first “comprehensive” 10-year agreement covering VMware software licenses, technical assistance and maintenance support. Financial terms were not disclosed. VMware Cloud Foundation will be at the core of the infrastructure. The deal targets three priorities: keeping services available during system upgrades, strengthening security and resilience, and accelerating the delivery of new services. Docomo will use the platform to expand capacity and manage traffic spikes, improve security patching and anomaly detection, and run virtual machines and containers on a common platform. Automation across development, testing and releases will help shorten the time needed to introduce new features. The companies also plan to expand AI-driven operations and prepare the infrastructure for future developments, including 6G and IOWN. The agreement comes a week after Tan’s comments at a Singapore panel, where he called capital the biggest constraint on further AI development as Broadcom works through wafer and memory shortages. “A lot of investors have no clue what they're investing in, but set very extreme expectations, only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino gambling,” Tan said when asked about cheaper AI models, Reuters noted. His remarks addressed investment into the broader AI sector. Tan also acknowledged that Anthropic and OpenAI had shown an ability to generate significant revenue from their latest models deployed for AI personal assistants. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk also subsequently responded, saying, “No crying in the casino,” weighing in on Tan’s concerns about speculative AI investments. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for AVGO slipped to ‘extremely bearish’ at 24/100 — its lowest levels in nearly 18 months — from ‘bearish’ levels a day ago amid a 300% surge in 24-hour message volumes. Retail interest in the stock has been rising, with the ticker’s watcher base up 8% over the past three months. One user said, “The biggest problem with this stock is lack Catalysts from Broadcom, the last news was on Oct 13 for VMware HyperArmor. But nothing after it.”  Another user said, “Each time they beat earnings and revenue estimates. Yet here we are down 15% in that time frame.” A separate user said, “trash news! Still headed lower,” shortly after the Docomo agreement. Other traders were still looking for a bounce. Another user said, “when we sell off early into the session typically we see a nice reversal in overnight session into premarket.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (CRWV) shares fell nearly 2% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. However, Cathie Wood's ARK Investment purchased 132,498 shares of the company on Monday despite the selloff. The asset manager’s ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought 102,280 CRWV shares on Monday for $6.3 million, according to its website. The firm also bought 30,218 shares of CRWV for $1.8 million through the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). The purchase comes as Wall Street and Main Street remain concerned about the company’s ballooning debt levels. CoreWeave reported $35.6 billion in total debt as of June 30, while its second-quarter net interest expense rose to $640 million from $267 million a year earlier. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook. MoffettNathanson slashed CRWV stock’s target to $89 from $107 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, citing its “staggering financial obligations.” BNP Paribas also cut its price target on CoreWeave to $117 from $169 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that it sees a continued deterioration in investor confidence amid its debt obligations. While higher financing costs could contain the company's ability to fund future growth, the shares are "seemingly discounting some liquidity concerns," the analyst reportedly said in a research note. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and set a price target of $106, implying upside of more than 73% from its last close. The firm said ongoing volatility in the credit market raises questions about whether CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and at what pace. However, Goldman also said the ongoing debate over demand for frontier vs. off-frontier intelligence, and CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered internal rate of return, are "biased to the upside" over the next 24 months because of tight supply. The analyst also said that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds. Last week, Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director analyst, said in an interview that the recent sell-off was an overreaction, as the broader AI demand story remains intact. “I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while also highlighting that the sharp drop has created an opportunity for investors. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for CRWV stock was ‘extremely bullish,’ even as message volumes surged 938% over 24 hours, according to platform data. One user said, “$CRWV $NBIS are moving in tandem.. absolutely nothing to see here…” The user added, “When the wrestling match ends, these are going straight up, meanwhile, you or I have zero say in it.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals (EYPT), CoreWeave (CRWV) and Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE) hit fresh 52-week lows Monday as a failed drug trial, debt refinancing concerns, and weaker full-year revenue expectations weighed on the stocks. EyePoint stock crashed 85%, while CoreWeave and Eos Energy stocks dropped 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals stock crashed to a record low of $0.4 after the company reported disappointing results from LUCIA, its second pivotal Phase 3 study of DURAVYU, an experimental treatment for wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The drug failed to show that it worked as well as aflibercept in protecting vision at Weeks 52 and 56, hurting its chances of approval for the eye condition. The setback prompted the company to lay off 53% of its workforce, with the restructuring expected to bring $30 million in annualized savings and incur about $9 million in severance expenses. EyePoint reported roughly $118 million in cash and equivalents as of Sept. 30 and plans to concentrate its remaining resources on Phase 3 studies of DURAVYU for diabetic macular edema (DME). However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’. CoreWeave stock fell to a new annual low of $59.25 as analysts cut price targets amid concerns about its debt obligations and reliance on external funding. BNP Paribas lowered its price target to $117 from $169 while retaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. MoffettNathanson cut its target to $89 from $107 and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating. The analysts highlighted the potential consequences of weaker investor confidence and expensive financing. CoreWeave needs capital to expand its data center infrastructure and support growing demand for computing capacity. Higher borrowing costs and limited access to capital markets could complicate its expansion plans and weigh on shareholder returns. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Eos Energy Enterprises stock touched a two-year low of $1.72 despite reporting preliminary third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $82 million to $83 million, a sequential growth of 19% to 21%. However, investors focused on the company’s expectation that 2026 revenue would land in the lower half of its previously announced $300 million to $350 million range. The updated outlook follows an earlier reduction in the company's revenue forecast in August. Eos has recorded eight consecutive quarters of improving gross margins, but its margins remain deeply negative as it works to increase production and improve manufacturing efficiency at its Thorn Hill facility. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’. So far this year, EYPT, CRWV and EOSE stocks have declined between 14% and 97%. content: Hess Midstream HESM rose 2.2% in Friday's trading as Raymond James raised its rating to Market Outperform from Market Perform with a $32 price target, saying its recent selloff following the Chevron CVX restructuring has created an attractive entry point for investors.
